events.continuity_hook: Continues the Columbus lab plan after the hospital answers the main setup and storage questions from the initial shortlist session.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound and return flight pattern, decide between the close hotel and the more reliable suite hotel, and select a window seat if booking allows.
events.scenario_brief: The Columbus hospital confirms the Thursday evening room walk-through can happen as late as 8:00 p.m., demo gear can stay locked in the lab overnight, and Saturday teardown is expected to end around 4:15 p.m. but could still run later. The late-afternoon nonstop from Tampa now lines up better than the cheaper connection that arrives close to midnight. The hospital-adjacent hotel remains convenient but has uneven recent reviews and unclear mini-fridge availability, while the better-rated suite hotel 15 minutes away confirms a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, with no hot tub.

events.continuity_hook: Follows the Columbus booking after the selected flight becomes less comfortable for the required Thursday evening lab access.
events.interaction_goal: Compare keeping the retimed nonstop against rebooking to a less convenient connection, set the order of airport, hospital, and hotel stops, and confirm the hotel will hold the room for a late arrival.
events.scenario_brief: A schedule update pushes the booked Thursday nonstop later, making the landing-to-walk-through window tighter if Kara goes to the hotel first. The hospital can keep the lab contact available until 8:45 p.m., but not later, and the earlier connecting option would require leaving Tampa before her faculty call is likely to end. The Sunday afternoon return is unchanged, and the suite hotel still has the confirmed room setup, but late check-in and the direct airport-to-hospital rideshare plan need to be verified.

events.continuity_hook: Closes out Columbus logistics once flights and lodging are set and only the local access plan remains to tighten.
events.interaction_goal: Lock the Thursday evening route, set Friday and Saturday morning departure times from the hotel, and make a practical food-and-room routine for the teaching days.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before travel, the hospital sends final arrival instructions: Kara must use the rehab loading entrance for the demo bag, visitor parking is on a different level than the main garage, and the Saturday teardown checklist now includes returning borrowed mats to storage. The flights and suite hotel remain in place, with the Sunday afternoon return still protecting against a rushed Saturday exit. The unresolved details are the Thursday airport-to-hospital timing, Friday morning departure buffer from the hotel, and whether she should arrange a simple grocery delivery after late check-in.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next larger professional-conference episode after the late-summer teaching trip is nearly wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare venue convenience against room reliability, and identify what the conference hotel and suite property need to confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Columbus lab, Kara receives the final program for an October pediatric therapy conference in Denver. She is scheduled to lead a Friday afternoon lab and wants to attend a Saturday morning session, so she needs a Wednesday arrival that leaves enough time to adjust and check materials. Flight choices split between a reasonable afternoon connection and a cheaper late-evening arrival. The official conference hotel is attached to the venue but only shows run-of-house bedding and no clear in-room refrigerator, while a better-rated suite hotel near light rail confirms a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and fitness access but says the pool and hot tub may be seasonal.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Denver conference plan once conference timing and hotel availability are specific enough for a booking decision.
events.interaction_goal: Choose whether to stay attached to the venue or keep the more predictable suite setup, book the flights around the Wednesday arrival and Sunday return, and handle seat selection where available.
events.scenario_brief: The Denver conference office confirms Kara can access the lab room Friday morning for setup and that Saturday sessions end by noon. The venue hotel block expires in 72 hours; it can guarantee a queen room only at a higher non-block rate and still cannot confirm a refrigerator. The suite hotel verifies the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and fitness room, but its pool and hot tub will be closed for the season. On flights, a Wednesday afternoon arrival is available, while the most comfortable return is Sunday afternoon rather than a tight Saturday departure after the conference.

events.continuity_hook: Revisits the Denver lodging choice after a lower-rate venue room and a temporary suite-hotel fitness closure change the trade-off before cancellation becomes costly.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to keep the suite hotel or switch to the venue block, verify any partner-gym access, and make sure the slightly earlier Sunday return still leaves a workable checkout and airport plan.
events.scenario_brief: Before the Denver hotel cancellation deadline, the venue block reopens at a lower rate, but the available room is still listed as run-of-house with no refrigerator confirmation. At the same time, the booked suite hotel announces that its fitness room will be under renovation for the first night, though the room amenities remain confirmed and a nearby partner gym may be available. The Sunday return flight has moved slightly earlier but remains in the afternoon, so the main question is whether the reopened venue rate is worth giving up the more reliable room routine.
